newsitem.title: MEXICO: ICA studies replacing Eurobond - source.
newsitem.headline: ICA studies replacing Eurobond - source.

text.p: Mexican construction company Empresas Ica is analyzing how it will refinance its $151 million Eurobond, which comes due in February 1998, a company official said on Tuesday.
Analysts said the company may issue a new Eurobond.

"We have the intention of refinancing it, but since it does not come due until early next year, we have time to analyze the different options," said a company director, who declined to be identified. The amount outstanding on the bond, which yields 9.75 percent, is $151 million after the company rebought some of the original amount in 1995.
While the company says it could retire the bond using its cash, analysts said the issue could also be refinanced with a similar Eurobond, of up to $200 million.

"They have told us they could issue paper in a range similar to that coming due, but they could also increase it up to $200 million to pay other short-term debt," said Hector Castillo, with ING Barings in New York.
The anticipated issue could be led by Chase and Bancomer, according to a recent report. However, some analysts said the company could float a Yankee bond instead.
